note: GameFAQs "Bonus Stage", also in other published notes. One of the seven codes the decoder compares before the checksum ($05:96C6, table $05:9703, stored in JP letters for both carts): $0550 = 1: one life, the bonus stage ($CCC0). typed with the pad in Mesen (US); the RAM it sets read back. The same code in the other cart: PONEJACK Dynablaster (Europe): typed in Mesen, the same result.

GameFAQs "Long Primer Time", also in other published notes. One of the seven codes the decoder compares before the checksum ($05:96C6, table $05:9703, stored in JP letters for both carts): $03ED = 105. typed with the pad in Mesen (US); the RAM it sets read back. The same code in the other cart: PBOMBOLD Dynablaster (Europe): typed in Mesen, the same result.

GameFAQs "Manual Detonator", also in other published notes. One of the seven codes the decoder compares before the checksum ($05:96C6, table $05:9703, stored in JP letters for both carts): $03EE = 1 (detonator); copied to the player at each stage start in NORMAL MODE only ($CE0C). typed with the pad in Mesen (US); the RAM it sets read back. The same code in the other cart: PACHINKO Dynablaster (Europe): typed in Mesen, the same result.

GameFAQs "Normal Primer Time", also in other published notes. One of the seven codes the decoder compares before the checksum ($05:96C6, table $05:9703, stored in JP letters for both carts): $03ED = 75, the power-on value. typed with the pad in Mesen (US); the RAM it sets read back. The same code in the other cart: PBOMBMAN Dynablaster (Europe): typed in Mesen, the same result.

effect: Demo recorder: the attract demo records pad 1 instead of playing
note: Mesen 2 cheat engine (Game Genie). ROM byte $D2F7 (JP $D263) is 1 = play the recorded demo ($05:9A01). Set to 0, the demo code stores (button, frame count) pairs at ($B9),Y, the demo's own ROM table, instead: in Mesen the demo stood still and the store at $05:9A22 ran on each button change (3 times in 3,000 frames; 0 without the code, 915 playback calls). On a cart those stores hit the MMC1 registers; the recorder needs RAM there (development hardware) Mesen 2, 12,000 frames of the title and attract demo with no input: JP AAVILZPA (switch $D263) and Dynablaster AENIPZPA (switch $D2F1) each ran the record store (JP $05:9A12, EU $05:9A22) 34 times; 0 without, and the US code AENIYZPA does nothing on either.

note: US $05:A874-$A882: mode 2 (BATTLE) with the Four Score flag $48 = 0 plays sound $04 and stays on the menu; $48 is set each frame when the Four Score signature matches ($07:C382). Japan's menu ($05:A818) has no check. In Mesen with no Four Score the US game stayed on the menu; with one it went to the match select, as Japan does without. Dynablaster (Europe) has no such check: with plain pads in Mesen BATTLE MODE went to the match select, as in Japan.

effect: Japan skips straight to the mode menu; the US game ignores Start until the intro is over (about 5 s)
note: US $05:A20D skips the A/Start test while the intro flag $0521 is set ($05:A19E, cleared at $05:A566 after about 285 frames); Japan ($05:A1FE) tests from the first frame. Start pressed 60 frames in, in Mesen. Image: US (left), Japan. Dynablaster (Europe) ignores it as the US game does (Start 60 frames in, still the intro 40 frames later).

effect: An unused Area 6 map: nearly all soft blocks, a different pillar grid and enemy positions
note: The map is (area - 1) x 2 + a variant from the table at $04:BB69 ($04:BBC9); map pointers at $04:BBF7. Area 6's variant row is all 1, so map 10 ($04:9EDE) is never used, and no mode or demo reaches it. JP has the same data 8 and 17 bytes lower. With the variant byte for 6-1 set to 0 (iNES file $13BA1, JP $13B89) and password 36363333, 6-1 loads it in Mesen. Image: the unused map (left), the real 6-1 (right). Dynablaster (Europe): the same bytes (variant table at iNES file $13BA4).

effect: Three samples heard only in the sound room: a click, a short hit and a looping phrase
note: Sounds go through $07:C8F5 (JP $C861); the game asks for samples 1E (stop) and 27 only, and the music's drums use the samples behind 1F, 21, 23-26, 28 and 29. 20 ($EE80, about 0.06 s, a click), 22 ($EBC0, about 0.09 s, a hit) and 2A ($F5C0, about 0.93 s, looping) are written to the sample address by the sound room alone. 20 and 22 recorded in BizHawk; the clip of 2A is built from its sample bytes, not recorded. Dynablaster (Europe): the same bytes.

effect: Kondoria, four frames: loaded at every stage but never drawn
note: The common sprite block (bank 1 $8000) is loaded to PPU $0000 at every stage start ($07:CBDD). Backgrounds always use $1000, so its tiles can only show as sprites, and the only routine that writes sprite tiles ($07:CCE4) takes them from records in ROM. No record in either version names $84-$8B or $94-$9B: a blue blob in four frames (two walking, one more, one wide-eyed). The game gives it no palette; the image uses sprite palette 3, a guess. Dynablaster (Europe): the same bytes.

effect: The ending's church cross is still in the US cartridge; only the map leaves it out
note: The ending's street is drawn from metatiles ($04:B826). The US street graphics ($01:B724) still hold the cross (tiles $60-$63) and metatile $39 that uses them; the US and JP street maps ($04:AE17, JP $04:ADB7) differ in one cell only, column 14 row 4, which is $39 in JP and sky in US. The image is the US data with that cell put back, in the game's palette as read in Mesen. Dynablaster (Europe) has the US map (no cross in its ending, Mesen) and the same street graphics, moved to $01:B3AC.
